{"self_assessment": "Impact
I built the bottom-line stretch of the fish early, then laid the back line from the middle out to the tail junction and carried it into the upper fork, which completed the picture. The finished outline is a clear fish: a nose, a curved back and belly, and a forked tail. By my inspection, all 131 standing dominoes were connected to the start.

Execution
I worked steadily and in sequence. I traced my strokes from the pad, inspected the run twice, once mid-build and once after the upper fork was laid, and confirmed that nothing was loose and that the only open ends were the two tail tips. I flagged the doubled section on the back, checked that it was still connected, and chose not to touch it, which avoided adding bump risk. I used no more dominoes than the table had.

Collaboration
I offered to take the back-to-tail stretch when I saw I was free, and told Priya she could stay put or help Maya. I asked Leo to check the gaps around the middle of the back, and he did. After the build I proposed that everyone keep their hands off the table, and the team agreed to that.

Leadership
I took the initiative on the tail-junction stretch and the upper fork without being asked. I gave clear status updates to the table and set the hands-off rule before the push. That kept the table coordinated and protected the finished piece until the push.", "my_share_percent": 35}
